skill.name: swarm-planner
skill.description: Creates dependency-aware implementation plans optimized for parallel multi-agent execution. The skill researches context, asks clarifying questions, writes a Markdown plan, and requests a review pass.
skill.summary: Creates dependency-aware implementation plans for parallel multi-agent execution.
skill.author: am-will

content.value_statement: Complex projects are hard to split across agents without ordering mistakes. This skill creates dependency-aware plans with explicit parallel execution waves.
actual_capabilities: Researches project architecture, existing patterns, dependencies, and frameworks before planning.
Requires current documentation lookup for external libraries, frameworks, and APIs.
Creates task plans with explicit IDs, dependencies, locations, validation, status, logs, and edited files.
Separates work into parallel execution waves based on task prerequisites.
Requests subagent review to find missing dependencies, ordering issues, and edge cases.
Saves the plan as a Markdown file in the current working directory.
limitations: It produces a plan only and instructs agents not to implement changes.
It depends on available documentation tools or web search for external APIs.
It may pause for clarification when scope, architecture, or constraints are unclear.
It does not execute or coordinate the planned tasks after the plan is written.

use_cases.title: Prepare parallel implementation plans
use_cases.description: Map a planned feature into ordered tasks, validation steps, and execution waves for multiple agents.

use_cases.title: Break down large code changes
use_cases.description: Convert a broad refactor or migration into smaller tasks with clear dependencies and review points.

use_cases.title: Coordinate agent handoffs
use_cases.description: Create a shared plan that tells agents which tasks can start immediately and which tasks must wait.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a small feature
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a single feature in one codebase.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use swarm-planner to create a dependency-aware plan for adding [feature] to this repository. Ask questions if scope or architecture is unclear.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a library migration
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request that needs current external documentation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use swarm-planner to plan a migration from [old library] to [new library]. Check current documentation before defining tasks and validation.

prompt_templates.title: Plan parallel service changes
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request across multiple services or packages.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use swarm-planner to split [project goal] across services [list services]. Include dependencies, parallel execution waves, risks, and test strategy.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a reviewed agent swarm
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for multi-agent execution with review before handoff.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use swarm-planner to create a reviewed implementation plan for [large initiative]. Save the plan, request subagent review, revise gaps, and return the final waves.

output_examples.input: Add password reset to an existing web app.
output_examples.output: A Markdown plan with independent research and schema tasks first, then service, API, UI, email, and integration test waves.

output_examples.input: Migrate an API client to a new SDK.
output_examples.output: A plan that starts with documentation review, identifies affected files, separates adapter updates from tests, and lists migration risks.

output_examples.input: Split a refactor across three coding agents.
output_examples.output: A dependency graph and wave table showing which agents can work immediately and which work must wait for shared interfaces.

best_practices: Provide repository context, target behavior, and constraints before invoking the skill.
Answer clarification questions before asking agents to execute the generated plan.
Review dependency waves against team ownership, release order, and testing requirements.
anti_patterns: Using the skill for urgent one-line fixes where a plan adds overhead.
Skipping documentation lookup for third-party libraries that may have changed.
Treating parallel waves as independent when they share hidden state or deployment order.

faq.question: Does this skill write code?
faq.answer: No. It creates an implementation plan and explicitly instructs agents not to implement the changes.

faq.question: Can it run outside Plan Mode?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill says it can run inside or outside Plan Mode when explicitly invoked.

faq.question: Why does it ask clarification questions?
faq.answer: It asks questions when scope, architecture, constraints, or priorities could reasonably be interpreted in multiple ways.

faq.question: Does it require Context7?
faq.answer: It prefers Context7 or an MCP documentation tool for external dependencies, with web search as a fallback.

faq.question: Which AI tools does it support?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: How does it choose parallel work?
faq.answer: Tasks with empty or already completed dependencies are grouped into the earliest possible execution wave.
